analysis.title: GS Flood - Market and Liquidity Update 11.18.2026
key_insights: S&P futures up 0.30% premarket on Wed 18 Nov 2026, rates +/- 1bp, 10yr at 5.10%.
Yesterday rates rallied 2-3bps across the curve on a risk-off flight-to-quality move, despite firmer retail sales data.
Tech was weak again, with NDX re-testing its local lows ahead of the NVDA earnings report.
Per Rich Privorotsky (Head of European One Delta Trading), NVDA beat and raised, guiding $130bn versus about $125bn expected, with zero China data centre compute in the numbers.
Privorotsky says the market would have liked a hint that Jensen could return to China, but NVDA shut that down.

GS rates desk says tactical demand for Treasuries is improving, even though yesterday's long-end buyback was far weaker than anticipated: 1.18bn accepted, 20% of announced capacity, versus the full 6bn taken in the previous operation.
Mortgages reversed into the late afternoon, moving from 1 tick wider to 2.5-3 ticks tighter from 3-5pm. The desk says the initial move wider matched the drop in risk from the tech outages.
Hedge funds and some asset managers bought more basis into the end of the day. Flows after NVDA earnings were muted, though basis gapped about 1-1.5 ticks tighter after 4:30pm.

In the mortgage stack, lower coupons lagged on better selling, both outright and via coupon swaps. Lowers were 1-1.5 ticks wider and the rest of the stack was 2-3 ticks tighter. Origination was light again at about 1.3bn.
FOMC minutes are due at 2pm. GS economists will look for the assumptions behind participants' economic outlooks and their views on the balance of risks.
GS Economics expects Italy 2027 real GDP growth of 0.5%, below consensus, on weaker consumption and slowing investment.

GS Economics says October core retail sales rose 0.6%, above expectations, with the level revised up sharply. Industrial production fell 0.4%, below expectations, on utilities. Q4 GDP tracking is now +2.4% and the October core PCE estimate is 0.29%.

GS Equity Research midday note says the S&P 500 is down 3% for the week as investors reassess the AI trade alongside peaking earnings, potentially peak AI investment and a tightening Fed. The S&P has already taken 4 turns off its P/E peak from earlier this year.
GS Equity Research notes that US BIS remote-access rule uncertainty around chip supply to China weighed on Asian stocks.

market_movers.rationale: Privorotsky says NVDA beat and raised with a $130bn guide versus about $125bn expected and no China data centre compute in the numbers. The market wanted a hint of a China return, which NVDA ruled out.

earnings_insights: NVDA (reported overnight, 11/17-18): guided $130bn versus approx $125bn expected (consensus, per Privorotsky). Beat and raise, with zero China data centre compute in the numbers. The report does not state whether the $130bn is revenue or another metric, or which period it covers.

Above expectations, with the level revised up sharply. GS says it shows resilience of the US consumer.
Below expectations, mostly on utilities, which is source data for consumption in GDP.
GS tracking estimate, raised after the retail sales report.
GS estimate for the October print.
GS forecast, below consensus, on weaker consumption and slowing investment.

risk_factors: Peaking earnings and potentially peak AI investment.
Uncertainty over US chip supply to China under the BIS remote-access rule.
Weak demand at the Treasury long-end buyback (20% of announced capacity used).
vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds and some asset managers bought mortgage basis into the end of the day.
The S&P 500 sold off almost 2% Monday and is down 3% for the week as of Tuesday midday.
geopolitical: US BIS remote-access rule and uncertainty around US chip supply to China, discussed in GS Equity Research's China Internet & AI models note.
